description: Calculate the molecular adsorption energy of H2O on the TiO2(110) surface.
user_prompt: Calculate the molecular adsorption energy of intact H2O on the stoichiometric TiO2(110) rutile surface (P4_2/mnm) at a fivefold-coordinated Ti site. Report the final adsorption energy Eads (in eV), defined as Eads = E(slab+H2O) - E(slab) - E(H2O).

references: Lindan, Harrison & Gillan, Phys. Rev. Lett. 80, 762 (1998)
method.modeling: Stoichiometric rutile TiO2(110) slab with at least 4 layers, vacuum >= 15 Angstrom, and a 3x2x1 or larger surface supercell; adsorb intact H2O through O at a fivefold-coordinated Ti site. Reference the adsorption energy to the clean stoichiometric slab plus gas-phase H2O.
method.rationale: Value is the half-monolayer molecular adsorption energy E_M from Lindan et al. 1998, converted from their positive binding-energy convention to the negative Eads convention used by this benchmark. The final state is intact H2O bound O-down at a fivefold Ti site; a dissociated OH + H final state is not the target for this prompt. The reference value was computed with PW91 rather than PBE+U, so the +/-0.20 eV absolute tolerance covers PW91-to-PBE(+U), coverage, slab-size, and orientation differences.
